translations.# Run your business with Gestion\nGestio:
# Run your business with Gestion
Gestion is a Nextcloud application designed to make invoicing simple, secure, and efficient for freelancers, micro-enterprises, and small businesses.

Key Features:
* Add and manage customer profiles
* Create and customize product entries
* Generate professional quotes and invoices in PDF format
* Generate electronic invoices in the Factur-X format
* Send PDFs directly by email from the application
* Store generated documents securely within your Nextcloud instance
* Track your business activities more efficiently

✨ Electronic invoicing is supported in France. Gestion can generate Factur-X invoices that combine a human-readable PDF with structured electronic invoice data.

Factur-X files can always be generated and downloaded without using an external platform. Each company can also select and configure a compatible approved electronic invoicing platform.

The PDF generation system has also been redesigned to improve document layout, styling, and compatibility.

Gestion integrates seamlessly with the Nextcloud ecosystem and keeps your business data under your control.

If you require adaptations to comply with your country's regulations, please open an issue on the GitHub repository.

translations.Enter the current quote status, for exam: Enter the current quote status, for example Draft, Sent, Accepted, Rejected or Expired. An accepted quote can become binding evidence of the agreement.

translations.Internal identifier of the Nextcloud use: Internal identifier of the Nextcloud user associated with the invoice. It is generated by the application and is not the legal invoice number.
translations.Enter the invoice number. In France, it: Enter the invoice number. In France, it is mandatory and must be unique within a chronological, continuous and gap-free sequence.
translations.Enter the actual delivery date or the da: Enter the actual delivery date or the date on which the service was completed. This date is mandatory on French invoices.
translations.Enter the payment due date. French busin: Enter the payment due date. French business invoices must state the due date or applicable payment terms.
translations.Select the expected payment method using: Select the expected payment method using the structured code: cash, cheque, credit transfer, payment card or SEPA credit transfer.
translations.Select the quote from which this invoice: Select the quote from which this invoice is created. This links the invoice to its accepted commercial terms and customer.
translations.Enter the internal document revision. Do: Enter the internal document revision. Do not reuse or alter the legal number of an issued French invoice; issue a corrective document when required.
translations.Enter the payment status, for example Pe: Enter the payment status, for example Pending, Paid, Partially paid, Overdue or Cancelled. Keep it consistent with the payment due date.
translations.Use the actions menu to open, download,: Use the actions menu to open, download, duplicate or delete the invoice. In France, issued invoices are accounting records and must be retained; do not delete them to correct an error.
translations.Enter the customer company or legal busi: Enter the customer company or legal business name. In France, the buyer identity must appear on invoices.
translations.Enter the customer first name. Use it wi: Enter the customer first name. Use it with the last name for an individual customer or contact.
translations.Enter the customer last name. In France,: Enter the customer last name. In France, an individual buyer must be identified by name on the invoice.
translations.Enter additional legal information to di: Enter additional legal information to display on customer documents, such as legal form, registration details or a specific legal notice.
translations.Enter the business identifier. For a Fre: Enter the business identifier. For a French business customer, use the 9-digit SIREN. The customer SIREN is required for French electronic invoicing where applicable from 1 September 2026.
translations.Enter the customer intra-Community VAT n: Enter the customer intra-Community VAT number when applicable. A French VAT number contains FR, a 2-digit key and the 9-digit SIREN. It is required on French invoices in particular when the business customer is liable for VAT, including reverse charge cases.
translations.Enter a customer contact phone number, p: Enter a customer contact phone number, preferably with its international country prefix. This is contact information and is not a general mandatory invoice field in France.
translations.Enter a valid customer email address use: Enter a valid customer email address used for contact and document delivery. This is not a general mandatory invoice field in France.
translations.Enter the street and number of the custo: Enter the street and number of the customer address. In France, the buyer address and any distinct billing address must appear on invoices.
translations.Enter the postal code for the customer a: Enter the postal code for the customer address. Use the 5-digit postal code for a standard French address.
translations.Enter the city or locality of the custom: Enter the city or locality of the customer address. It forms part of the mandatory buyer address on French invoices.
translations.Enter the customer country using its ISO: Enter the customer country using its ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, for example FR for France. Country information is required for structured electronic invoice addresses.
translations.Use this column to delete the customer r: Use this column to delete the customer record. Deletion cannot be used to replace legally required invoice retention.
translations.This section provides information pertai: This section provides information pertaining to the use of this application under the legal framework applicable in various countries.

translations.Enter a unique internal reference or SKU: Enter a unique internal reference or SKU used to identify the product or service consistently.
translations.Enter a precise description of the suppl: Enter a precise description of the supplied product or service. A clear designation is mandatory on French invoices.
translations.Enter the unit price before VAT in the c: Enter the unit price before VAT in the configured invoice currency. The unit price excluding VAT is mandatory on French invoices when line details are required.
translations.Enter the applicable VAT rate as a numbe: Enter the applicable VAT rate as a number, for example 20 for 20 percent. French invoices must distinguish the applicable VAT rate and related tax amount when VAT applies.
translations.Choose S for VAT at 5.5%%, 10%% or 20%%;: Choose S for VAT at 5.5%%, 10%% or 20%%; E for a VAT-exempt supply, then verify its exemption reason in Actions; Z for a legally zero-rated taxable supply; O for an operation outside the scope of VAT; AE for reverse charge; G for export outside the EU; or K for an intra-Community supply.
translations.Use this button to turn the product into: Use this button to turn the product into a description row in a quote.
translations.For category E, use this column to selec: For category E, use this column to select the VAT exemption reason. You can also delete the product or service from the catalogue.

translations.Electronic invoicing is only for busines: Electronic invoicing is only for businesses in France. If your business is not based in France, you can still generate and download simple PDF invoices.
translations.Factur-X generation and download remain: Factur-X generation and download remain available even when no platform is selected. You can chose your preferred platform.

translations.If you benefit from the VAT basic exempt: If you benefit from the VAT basic exemption — a common situation for micro-entrepreneurs — “VAT not applicable, art. 293 B of the French General Tax Code” is already selected. You do not need to change anything.
translations.If your exemption is based on another pr: If your exemption is based on another provision, select the corresponding reason. If in doubt, contact your accountant or the tax authorities.
